proposition: One Transit Backpack, packed once, holds everything it takes to get home — thirty litres deep.

board.style_line: Photoreal live-action film frame, vertical 9:16, hard equatorial midday sun as the single light source arriving high from camera-left with a bright sand bounce as the only fill, bleached coral shore and cold grey-green sea graded down to near-neutral so one saturated colour remains in the frame and it is the backpack's bright yellow lining, clean undistorted optics, no stylisation, no grain, no colour cast beyond the sun —
board.negative_line: — no text, no letters, no numerals, no captions, no subtitles, no logos, no brand marks, no watermarks, no signage, no labels, no printed packaging, no weapon pointed at any person, no blood, no recognisable real person or celebrity likeness, no film-poster or movie-key-art styling, no ancient-Greek costume, armour, sandals, columns, galleys or laurel wreaths, no second bag, no saturated colour anywhere except the yellow lining, no lens flare, no speed blur on the product.

identity_anchors.transit_backpack: deep navy matte body, bright yellow lining, vertical front zip and front bucket pocket with two black zip pulls, black padded straps, small top grab handle
identity_anchors.castaway: a sun-darkened South Asian man in his late thirties, matted shoulder-length hair, short salt-stiff beard, a faded bleached cotton shirt worn open over a vest, drawstring trousers cut short, bare feet, no jewellery, no tattoos, no armour and no costume of any period
identity_anchors.shore: a narrow bleached coral-sand shore with driftwood and dry palm fronds, cold grey-green sea always on frame right, pale overexposed sky at the top of the frame, no buildings, no boats but one lashed driftwood raft, no other people

hero_frame.description: The deep navy matte backpack stood upright and open on wet coral sand, its bright yellow lining full of light, and laid out around it on the sand in one wide readable arc: a coil of tarred rope, a folded fishing net, two coconuts, a dented tin, a small brass compass, a rolled bleached shirt, a flint, and one small photograph lying face-up. Rising out of the main compartment and still coming, a lashed driftwood-and-cord fishing spear already longer than the bag is tall. The man crouches behind the arc, small in the top third of the vertical frame but large enough to read on a phone, so his body gives the bag its scale. Nothing in the frame is text and nothing in the frame is a claim: the whole argument is the visible arithmetic between one thirty-litre bag and everything that came out of it.

audio.music_bed: No music at all for the first 12.5 s — location sound only: wet sand, one gull, wind, low surf and a single long zip run. At 12.5 s, after the photograph has already made the feeling, one sustained cello note enters under a sparse plucked figure, stays unresolved through the packing and the walk, and settles onto one low note as he clears frame at 27.0 s. Because no music plays before 12.5 s, the opening sets no register the film then fails to keep. No jingle, no song, no vocal.

beats.title: Sand gives it up
beats.feeling: A jolt of recognition — something that belongs to the life he lost is lying in the place he is stuck in.
beats.framing: Very tight, very low: 35 mm at ankle height, camera static, shore landward side of the action line with the sea a thin cold band top-right. The bottom two-thirds of the vertical frame is wet coral sand. A bare cracked hand enters from frame left and drags a black padded strap and the deep navy matte body of the backpack up out of the sand, left to right, sheeting wet sand off the matte navy. Sparse frame, so one edge treatment only: tight fit with a deliberate slight gap under the hand. One attention cue: the drag. Reads — 1) the navy mass breaking the sand, 2) the black strap and the small top grab handle, 3) the cold sea band at the top edge.
beats.first_frame: Before anything moves: an unbroken plane of wet coral sand with one black padded strap and the small black top grab handle of the deep navy matte backpack just breaking the surface, the buckle catching the sun. No hand yet, no man, no horizon, no island. The frame is a surprise, not an establishing shot.
beats.impact: Camera static because the object supplies the movement; a move here would only cover up. High key, one nameable fictional source — the midday sun high camera-left — and one consistent direction held for the whole film. The navy body is declared matte (diffuse) so it holds its tone under hard light; the black straps sit in the family of angles of the sand bounce and are lit as if they were metal, so black reads against navy instead of merging. Sound: the wet suck of sand, one gull, no music. The shot ends on the movement of the strap, which is what motivates the cut out of it.

beats.title: The yellow
beats.feeling: Relief that has a colour — the first good thing to happen on this shore in years, and it happens in one pull.
beats.framing: Cut round the arc about 45° and change lens: 50 mm, static, chest height. The bag stands upright in the lower off-centre zone of the 9:16 frame with pale sky at the top end of the long axis — two elements opposed at the two ends of the long axis, which is what makes the vertical frame mean tallness rather than merely being tall. His hand runs the vertical front zip down the full height of the front panel in one unhurried pull; the front bucket pocket falls open and bright yellow lining floods the centre of the frame. Sparse frame, tight fit. One attention cue: colour. Reads — 1) the yellow mouth of the pocket, 2) the two black zip pulls swinging apart, 3) his shoulder soft behind.
beats.first_frame: The deep navy matte backpack standing upright on wet sand, closed, both black zip pulls seated together at the foot of the vertical front zip, a hand just arriving at the top of the pull. No yellow anywhere in the frame yet — navy, grey sand, pale sky only.
beats.impact: Static 50 mm; the zip carries the motion, so the camera is held by choice. This is the closer shot that ties the colour to the product, so that a small yellow flash in any later, wider or busier frame reads as this bag and nothing else; the ground is graded down precisely so that one hue is nearly the only colour present. The yellow lining is matte and lit by sand bounce — no specular on it, no highlight competing with the two glossy black zip pulls, which keep the frame's only direct reflections. Sound: one long, crisp, unhurried zip run — the audio burr, and the only clean man-made sound on the island. The composed line 'Transit Backpack' arrives at 4.2 s over this beat, which puts the name inside ten seconds without displacing the surprise from frame one.

beats.title: It keeps coming
beats.feeling: Delighted disbelief — the laugh, and the laugh is the selling point rather than a decoration on it.
beats.framing: Cut wider and about 50° further round: 28 mm, low, static except for one slow six-degree tilt up motivated entirely by the object in transit. The open bag sits in the lower third; the arc of what has already come out of it lies round it; out of the main compartment a lashed driftwood-and-cord fishing spear keeps sliding, longer than the bag, then longer than the man. Busy frame, so by rule the edges stop mattering and no edge treatment is claimed. One attention cue: the emerging spear. Reads — 1) the yellow mouth of the bag, 2) the impossible length of the spear crossing the long axis, 3) the arc of goods and, small but findable, the crouched man giving scale.
beats.first_frame: The hero frame: the deep navy matte backpack upright and open on wet coral sand, bright yellow lining full of light, an arc laid round it of tarred rope, folded net, two coconuts, a dented tin, a small brass compass, a rolled shirt, a flint and one small photograph face-up, and the spear already risen a bag's height out of the main compartment. The man crouches behind the arc, small enough to sit in the top third and large enough to read at phone size.
beats.impact: The expectation being violated is the category's fixed picture of a castaway: a man with nothing. This frame is a man with everything, because he packed well — the borrowed image is re-angled onto the product advantage rather than set down unmodified beside a logo. The frame is busy, so it holds its describe-aloud length: five seconds is the longest hold in the film and still slightly under what the arc would take to say aloud, which is a declared cost of the thirty-second cap. The spear is fishing gear — lashed cord, driftwood shaft, blunt bone point, never lifted and never pointed at a person — so the brief's joke lands as a tool, not a weapon. The composed '30L' arrives at 9.4 s against the pale sky at the top end of the long axis: the figure and the picture make the same point at the same moment. Sound: the rattle of goods, then one long dry wooden slide that runs past the point of belief. Still no music.

beats.title: Her face, face up
beats.feeling: The reason. The laugh drops into something quiet without the film changing its mind about what it is.
beats.framing: The tightest shot in the film: 85 mm, static, shallow. Two salt-wet hands pick the small photograph off the sand and turn it. The photograph is seen from behind and over its top edge only — the woman is never rendered legibly, only the shape of her hair and one shoulder at the frame's edge. Frame left, soft and out of focus, a wedge of deep navy matte and one thumb of bright yellow lining, so the product does not lapse for a single beat. One attention cue: the turn of the photograph. Reads — 1) the photograph's white border, 2) his thumbprint of wet sand on it, 3) the blurred navy and yellow at the edge.
beats.first_frame: The small photograph lying face-down on wet coral sand, one corner curled stiff with salt, two fingertips just reaching its edge. Beside it, out of focus, a wedge of deep navy matte body and a sliver of bright yellow lining.
beats.impact: Static 85 mm — the held camera is the choice, not laziness, and no focus is racked: the shallow plane is set once and the hands come to it. He has turned into the shade of a driftwood stump, so the exposure level drops about half a stop while the fictional source stays the same sun in the same direction; the level follows the dramatic line, not a brightness slider. Every other sound is withdrawn — no sand, no gulls — leaving only wind and low surf, which the ear then listens to for meaning as though it were speech. The single cello enters here and only here, after the feeling has already been made out of the picture. Nothing in this beat names or resembles any published character, and the woman is not a recognisable likeness.

beats.title: He packs
beats.feeling: Competence — the ordinary, specific pleasure of a bag taking everything you own and still closing.
beats.framing: Cut back out: 40 mm, static, chest height, line unbroken — sea still frame right, the man still working frame left of the bag as he has since frame one. Hands and forearms occupy the top half, the bag the lower half. In they go in order: coconuts, tin, flint, compass, folded net, rolled shirt; the photograph last and into the front bucket pocket; the vertical front zip closes over the yellow; the spear is lashed along one side under a compression strap. Busy but ordered frame; one attention cue: the closing zip line. Reads — 1) the yellow seam shutting, 2) the two black zip pulls meeting at the foot, 3) the spear shaft crossing the frame.
beats.first_frame: The bag seen from the front, open, empty and yellow-lined, the arc of goods restacked into a neat pile at frame right, one coconut already in his hand at the top edge of the frame.
beats.impact: Static 40 mm; all the motion is inside the frame, which is the product performing rather than the camera pointing at it. The bag is shown in use and its end result is shown in the same beat — everything in, and it still closes. The zip shuts in one shorter pull that rhymes with the long one in beat 2. Music continues, unresolved. The cut out of this shot is motivated by the click of the side-strap buckle, which also carries across the cut as a sound bridge.

beats.title: He goes
beats.feeling: Departure, and its cause — the thing he packed is the thing getting him out.
beats.framing: The widest shot in the film and the first time the shore is seen whole: 24 mm, static, low. Sea frame right exactly as it has been since frame one. He walks away from camera into the shallows towards frame right with the packed bag on his back — black padded straps on his shoulders, small top grab handle uppermost — and a lashed driftwood raft waits at the water's edge. The bag is the darkest mass in a pale frame and separates from its ground in grayscale without relying on hue; one thumb of bright yellow shows at the top of the closed vertical zip. Off-centre placement, subject and setting together. One attention cue: his walk. Reads — 1) the navy bag against the bleached shore, 2) the stride into water, 3) the horizon at the top end of the long axis.
beats.first_frame: The empty pale shore, sea frame right, the driftwood raft at the water's edge, and the man just entering from the bottom-left corner with the packed navy backpack already on his back — the first frame in the film in which the bag is worn.
beats.impact: Static 24 mm; stillness is the choice, because a move here would be the camera covering up a shot that is already doing its job. Screen direction is unbroken — everything in this film has travelled left to right towards the sea — so no bridging insert is needed and no setup has crossed the line. This cut does give up three-dimensional continuity: we never saw the raft being built. That is a sacrifice taken from the bottom of the list, keeping emotion, story and rhythm intact. Sound: surf rises, feet enter water, the buckle click from the outgoing shot is explained by the incoming one; the cello settles onto one low note as he clears frame.

beats.title: The pack, and the address
beats.feeling: The quiet after the joke — the last thing in the viewer's eye is the object, not the gag.
beats.framing: No generated motion: code holds the final still of beat 6, cross-dissolves over eight frames — a dissolve chosen at jump-cut length so it reads as a hard join rather than as a superimposition, never the software default — and composes the close. The packed deep navy matte backpack stands alone, three-quarter front, on the same wet sand against the pale sea, in the lower-centre zone of the 9:16 frame; the supplied mokobara_wordmark SVG is placed unaltered in the upper zone with clear space round it; 'Transit Backpack', '30L' and 'mokobara.com' are composited beneath it as real text on the text layer, never generated into the picture. The product angle is the one showing the most surfaces — front panel, one side panel, and the top with its grab handle.
beats.first_frame: The packed navy backpack upright and three-quarter front on wet sand, front bucket pocket zipped, both black zip pulls seated at the foot of the vertical front zip, one thumb of bright yellow lining showing at the top, pale sea and sky behind, nothing else in frame.
beats.impact: Held still for the full 2.5 s — longer than its content strictly needs to be read, deliberately, because it is the last thing the viewer holds and the only place the action is asked for. One last zip click, then room tone; the cello has already resolved, so nothing competes with the address. The film ends on the pack.

name_super.why: Attribution fails by default, so the name lands inside ten seconds — but after frame one, so the surprise keeps the gate and the name keeps the credit. Placed in the lower zone over the band of wet dark sand beneath the bag, aligned to the horizontal structure of the waterline underneath it. Warm off-white (#F5F1E8) at 44 px on a 1080-wide delivery, medium weight, mixed case, no thin strokes, no all-caps: measured against the darkest and the lightest pixels under the letters the ratio runs 11.4:1 to 6.2:1, so it clears 4.5:1 at every point of its ground and does not rely on the large-text carve-out.

capacity_super.why: The one specific figure, released at the exact moment the spear is still coming out, so the number and the picture argue together rather than the number explaining the picture. Placed at the top end of the long axis against the pale sky, opposing the bag at the bottom end. Deep ink (#101820) at 72 px, medium weight: measured under the letters the ratio runs 14.1:1 against the brightest sky and 5.8:1 where a cloud darkens it, clearing 4.5:1 throughout. '30L' is a unit, not a running line, so the mixed-case rule is not engaged.

close_card.why: The ask, made once, plainly, at the end, on the pack. Three type sizes only, each a rank: the supplied wordmark placed unaltered at the top of the zone, 'Transit Backpack' beneath it, then '30L' and 'mokobara.com' on one baseline below. Deep ink on the pale sea-and-sky band; measured under the letters the ratio runs 12.6:1 to 5.1:1 at the darkest point of the water. The wordmark is the supplied SVG, placed and never redrawn, restyled or regenerated; where the band under it falls below 3:1 the brand's own higher-contrast variant is used, never an author recolour.

mandatory.customer_words: lets make an ad with mokobara
mandatory.realisation: A single 30 s Mokobara film whose only subject is one Mokobara product: the Transit Backpack is on screen in all seven beats, is the object every action is performed on, and is the last thing in frame. Nothing else in the film is branded.

mandatory.customer_words: i would preferably give it the odysey movie angel
mandatory.realisation: The shape only — a man held years on an island, a picture of the wife he is trying to get back to, a long way home — carried across beats 1, 3, 4 and 6. It is the oldest story shape in circulation and is used as a shape, with no line, name, image, character, costume, prop or design element taken from any film or published telling.

The bag is his and was packed before he was stranded — that is the film's whole premise and the source of the joke. Beat 1 shows it coming out of the sand of the shore he was kept on, not arriving from anywhere, so it reads as something he already owned rather than something washed up.

mandatory.customer_words: the protagonist found his mokobara bag, while he was on the island where he was kept for years
mandatory.realisation: Beats 1 and 2: his hand drags the buried navy body out of wet sand, and the first pull of the vertical front zip opens the yellow lining. The years are carried in his state — matted hair, salt-stiff beard, bleached clothes, bare feet — not in a caption or a montage.

mandatory.customer_words: in that bag he founds her wives photo
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4, the tightest shot in the film: a small photograph turned over in two salt-wet hands. Seen from behind and over its top edge only, so the woman is never a legible or recognisable likeness. It is the film's emotional centre and it is the one item put back last, into the front bucket pocket, in beat 5.

mandatory.customer_words: and a lot of stuff that he could use to go back
mandatory.realisation: Beat 3, the hero frame: rope, fishing net, two coconuts, a dented tin, a brass compass, a rolled shirt, a flint and the spear laid out in one readable arc around a bag that plainly should not have held them. Each item is something the return actually needs, so the arc is an inventory rather than a gag prop list.

mandatory.customer_words: he packs food and stuff and goes back
mandatory.realisation: Beat 5 is the packing, in order, ending with the zip closing over the yellow and the spear lashed along the side; beat 6 is the going — bag worn on his back, into the shallows towards the raft, frame right, the same direction everything has travelled since frame one.

mandatory.customer_words: would be funny that he could keep his arms in the bag and food and so much stuff
mandatory.realisation: The film's one joke and its one selling point are the same thing: a thirty-litre bag that keeps giving. In beat 3 a lashed driftwood-and-cord fishing spear slides out of the main compartment past the length of the bag, then past the length of the man; the coconuts and the tin make the food half of the line in beats 3 and 5. The spear is handled as fishing gear — blunt bone point, never raised, never pointed at a person — so the joke lands without a weapon in an Indian-market ad. Register is warm and dry, not slapstick; ASCI code check sits outside Canon and is owed on this beat before release.

mandatory.customer_words: Avoid getting copyright violoations from odysssey
mandatory.realisation: Nothing nameable is used. No title, character name, actor likeness, line of dialogue, score, poster composition or key-art styling from any film; no Greek-antiquity costume, armour, sandals, galley, columns or laurel; no cyclops, no sirens, no bow, no loom, no named places. The castaway is unnamed in the film and unnamed in the copy, and the only words on screen are the three the brief supplied. The negative line blocks all of the above at prompt level on every beat.

Every beat is framed 9:16 and the vertical is earned by a named shape rather than by the platform: the standing bag, the full-height vertical front zip, the standing man and the rising spear all run along the long axis, and each beat opposes two elements at its two ends — bag low against sky high in beats 2, 3 and 6.

Six generated clips of 3.5, 4.0, 5.0, 4.5, 5.0 and 5.5 s, contiguous, plus a code-composed 2.5 s close at clip_s 0: 30.0 s exactly. Native audio is on and designed per beat — location sound only to 12.5 s, then one cello line — and the film is built to read with the sound off as well, since every beat is a visible action and all three strings are composited.

One film, seven beats, one continuous story with a want, an obstacle and a stated stake. Every shot is generated as a still and driven to motion image-to-video, stitched by code; the close is composed by code from the final still.

mandatory.customer_words: "entity_id": "mokobara_transit_backpack_private_island"; identity_invariants: "deep navy matte body", "bright yellow lining", "vertical front zip and front bucket pocket with two black zip pulls", "black padded straps, small top grab handle"
mandatory.realisation: The four invariants are restated verbatim as the transit_backpack identity anchor in every prompt, and each one is given at least one beat where it is the read: the top grab handle and a black padded strap in beat 1, the vertical front zip and the yellow lining in beat 2, the front bucket pocket in beats 3 and 5, both black zip pulls in beats 2, 5 and 7, the padded straps worn in beat 6, the matte navy body throughout. The navy is declared matte and never rendered glossy; the reference product photograph governs proportion, panel seams and pull shape.

mandatory.customer_words: exact_text_strings: "Transit Backpack", "30L", "mokobara.com" — placement overlay, script latin, may_reflow false
mandatory.realisation: All three carried verbatim on the text layer and never reflowed: 'Transit Backpack' at 4.2–7.2 s, '30L' at 9.4–12.4 s, and all three on the close card at 27.5–30.0 s. No prompt quotes any word to be rendered, and the negative line forbids letters and numerals inside every generated frame, so no message word exists only as generated pixels.

mandatory.customer_words: reference_assets: mokobara_wordmark (role: logo, image/svg+xml), transit_backpack_private_island_1 (role: product, image/jpeg)
mandatory.realisation: The wordmark SVG is placed unaltered on the close card — never redrawn, recoloured, regenerated or given a generated substitute — and appears nowhere inside a generated frame. The product JPEG is the likeness reference for every still, so the bag on the shore is a recognisable likeness of the real one rather than a navy backpack in general.

Copy is originated in English, not translated, and no Devanagari or other Indic glyph is generated anywhere. The target India is named by more than one variable rather than inherited: metro and tier-one salaried and self-employed buyers aged roughly 25–40 who fly or train four to eight times a year, read English by default, and pay a premium for design — not 'India', not 'the masses', not a town-size stratum. The castaway is cast South Asian and the humour is situational rather than verbal or regional, so it needs no local idiom to land.

No peril, no injury, no blood, no weapon aimed at a person, no real person's likeness, no religious or national symbol, no claim beyond the one figure the brief supplied. The spear is fishing gear and is handled as such. The brief's own copyright instruction is honoured at prompt level rather than at review level.

brand_timeline.in_context: The product itself is the branding and it never lapses: the Transit Backpack is in frame from 0.0 s to 30.0 s, in every one of the seven beats, with at least one of its four identity invariants as a primary read in each. The composed name 'Transit Backpack' arrives at 4.2 s — inside ten seconds, and after the surprise rather than in place of it. The supplied wordmark SVG appears once, at 27.5 s, on the close card, placed and unaltered. More than one branding asset carries the brand: product shot (beats 1–5), in-situ wear (beat 6), pack shot and wordmark (beat 7).
brand_timeline.spoken: none — the production constraint forbids dialogue and voice-over, so the brand name is never spoken and the on-screen channel carries it alone. Declared in deviations.

last_frame: The packed deep navy matte Transit Backpack standing upright and three-quarter front on wet coral sand against the pale sea, front bucket pocket zipped, both black zip pulls seated at the foot of the vertical front zip, one thumb of bright yellow lining showing at the top and the small top grab handle uppermost, with the supplied mokobara wordmark placed unaltered above it and 'Transit Backpack', '30L' and 'mokobara.com' composited beneath.

deviations.from: and its pre-arbitrated conflict (mla_0064 vs ogx_0032): default no humour; humour only where a brief clause asks, the register fits product and audience, and the joke carries the selling point — record it.
deviations.brief_clause: "would be funny that he could keep his arms in the bag and food and so much stuff" — the customer's own words ask for the comic register. The joke is not decoration: the thing that is funny (a thirty-litre bag that keeps producing) is the thing being sold, so humour and the selling point are the same object. Register is set by product and audience per whip_0058 — warm, dry, situational, no slapstick, no cartoon, no vignette parade, one joke told once. ogx_0032's execution bound is accepted: if the comic beat cannot be made to land in the single pull of beat 3, the film loses nothing by playing the reveal straight, because the arithmetic in the hero frame sells with or without the laugh.

deviations.from: , and (say the name as well as show it; the on-screen CTA is voiced in the same words) and / (brand richly across asset types including voice-over; pair every super with a matching audio line).
deviations.brief_clause: The job's standing production constraint: "no dialogue or voice-over." With no spoken channel available, the name, the figure and the ask are carried by the on-screen channel alone and by the product's own continuous presence. The corpus states plainly that it does not say how this is done on a sound-off or voice-less delivery, so this is a declared gap, not a solved one: the compensation is that the brand is the object in every frame, and the supers are timed to moments the picture is already making.

deviations.from: and : flag one named person — put the buyer's name, or a name, in the work.
deviations.brief_clause: "Avoid getting copyright violoations from odysssey", read together with the job's constraint on "no named film, actor, character or copyrighted work" and 's own prohibition on an invented person. Naming the hero would either borrow a protected name or invent one, and both are barred. The requirement is carried instead by the other half of the same decision: one specific figure ('30L'), and sensory detail attached to one individual rather than to a category — salt-stiff beard, wet sand thumbprint, the curled corner of one photograph.

deviations.from: and whip_0013 ( in concept_and_distinctiveness): the conflict is the product's absence; dramatising life without the product usually beats dramatising life with it.
deviations.brief_clause: "the protagonist found his mokobara bag, while he was on the island where he was kept for years" — the brief's premise is the finding, so the product is on screen from frame one. The deprivation is kept, but placed before the film: the years without it are legible in the man's hair, beard, bleached clothes and bare feet, and in the empty shore itself. The obstacle is the sea and the distance, never the buyer's own defect and never a rival.

deviations.from: and gote_0053 ( in editing_pacing_and_short_form): a shot that must be read holds at least its describe-aloud duration.
deviations.brief_clause: "seconds": 30. The hero frame in beat 3 carries nine items plus the bag plus the scale figure; said aloud it runs past five seconds. It is cut at 5.0 s, the longest hold in the film. The cost is declared and mitigated rather than hidden: the arc is staged as one readable line instead of a scatter, the spear's motion draws the eye along that line, and the 2.5 s close card re-reads the product alone at the end.
